plotter.py.summary: Plot a mathematical expression and save it as ``plot.png``.
details: Accepts ``f(x)=<expression>`` on the command line, evaluates it over ``-10..10`` with numpy (sin, cos, tan, sqrt, exp, log, pi and e are available) and renders a labelled Matplotlib figure to ``plot.png`` at 300 dpi.

plow.py.summary: Render a Markdown file (or stdin) in the terminal with rich.
details: Prints the text through ``rich``, renders fenced code blocks with syntax highlighting and line numbers (Monokai theme) and can page long documents with a system pager.

ppage.py.summary: Split PDFs into one file per page, or extract their text page by page.
details: Uses PyMuPDF on the PDFs named on the command line (or below the current directory) and writes the pages concurrently; ``-t`` writes the per-page text instead of single-page PDFs.

pret.py.summary: Format web and Markdown files in place with prettier.
details: Runs ``prettier -w`` over the given files, or over every ``.html``/``.js``/``.ts``/``.tsx``/``.md``/``.scss``/``.coffee`` file below the current directory, skipping empty and single-line files and rewriting the Android ``/storage/emulated/0`` prefix to ``/sdcard``. Files are processed in parallel.

pret2.py.summary: Format JavaScript, CSS, HTML, JSON and TypeScript files with prettier.
details: Walks the current directory for the supported extensions (``.min.js``/``.min.css``/``.d.ts`` excluded), runs prettier on each file with a timeout in a worker pool, and moves the files that fail into an ``error`` folder with a unique name. A summary of changed/failed files is printed at the end.

prompt-reformatter.py.summary: Reflow long prompt text files to 80 columns on list and sentence boundaries.
details: Splits the content before numbered items, bullet points, bold headings and commas, re-wraps the lines that exceed ``MAX_LINE`` at semicolons and rewrites every ``.txt`` file below the current directory that changes.

purepy.py.summary: Classify PyPI packages as pure Python or as shipping native extensions.
details: Reads the package names from a file, queries the PyPI JSON API for the available wheel tags (in a worker pool) and writes ``pure_python.txt``, ``native_extensions.txt`` and ``not_found.txt`` with the classification.

py7zmax.py.summary: Compress a single file into a ``.7z`` archive with maximum LZMA2 settings.
details: Writes ``<name>.7z`` with the LZMA2 filter at preset 9 plus the extreme flag, replaces the file atomically and removes the original once the archive is complete. Existing archives are never overwritten.

py_dev.py.summary: Scaffold a new Python project with linting, tests and CI.
details: Creates the package layout, ``pyproject.toml``, ``.gitignore``, a pre-commit configuration (ruff, black, isort, mypy, the standard hooks), a pytest test and a GitHub Actions workflow, then installs the development requirements and initialises the virtual environment. The project directory can be passed as the first argument, otherwise the prompts ask for it.

pyco.py.summary: Delete every ``__pycache__`` directory below the current directory.
details: Removes the bytecode caches with :func:`shutil.rmtree` and prints how many directories were deleted and how much space was freed.

pycppcheck.py.summary: Syntax-check C and C++ sources with clang in parallel.
details: Runs ``clang -fsyntax-only`` for ``.c``/``.h``/``.inc`` files and ``clang++ -fsyntax-only`` for the C++ extensions, over the files on the command line or below the current directory, and prints one OK/error line per file from a spawn-based pool.

pycurl_downloader.py.summary: Download the URLs of a list into ``downloads/`` with pycurl.
details: Reads the URLs from a file, fetches them concurrently with pycurl (30 s timeout, browser user agent), derives the file name from the URL and writes the failures to a ``failed`` list for a retry.

pyfslint.py.summary: Scan a directory tree for filesystem problems.
details: Individual checks (also selectable one by one, ``--all`` runs everything) report duplicate files, badly named entries, non-UTF-8 names, broken symlinks, empty directories, bad UID/GID ownership, non-stripped binaries, shadowed ``PATH`` executables, temporary/junk files, world-writable items and names with redundant whitespace. ``--summary`` adds a one-line result table; the docstring doubles as the ``--help`` text.

pygdu.py.summary: Interactive disk-usage browser in the terminal.
details: Scans the given directory with a worker pool, shows the entries as a navigable list with size bars and lets you descend into folders or go back with the arrow keys and Enter/Escape.
